newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in Europe, Asia.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in Europe, Asia.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - British shares finished lower but well above the day's worst levels as Wall Street stocks turned higher after a choppy start. The FTSE, still under the spell of Wall Street after last Friday's sell-off, ended 18.3 points lower at 3,972.4 a gain of 9.4 from last Friday.

FRANKFURT - German shares close bourse trade just off session lows amid nervousness over Wall Street. The DAX index ended down 47.37 points at 2,799.71 a rise of 7.81 since last Friday. In post-bourse trade the index fell 31.17 to 2,815.77.

PARIS - French stocks closed lower but above their session lows after Wall Street appeared to be recovering from the previous day's slide, which triggered sell-offs in equities markets around the world. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 8.70 points, or 0.39 percent, at 2,203.41, down 37.31 from a week ago.
ZURICH - Swiss shares closed lower after Wall Street posted early losses. The all share SPI fell 10.56 points to close at 2,454.67 up 4.00 since last week.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key benchmark bounced back somewhat by the end of the session to above the 20,000 threshold after plunging by nearly 550 points earlier due to weakness on Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 finished down 159.81 points, or 0.78 percent, at 20,341.39, up 64.69 since last Friday.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks slid to a weak close, dragged down chiefly by nervousness in the outlook for international equity markets. The Hang Seng Index closed down 269.21 points, or 2.06 percent, at 12,784.07, a drop of 318.66 on the week.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended with its third consecutive fall in response to the overnight plunge on Wall Street, but investors regained some confidence in the afternoon session. The All Ordinaries index closed 23.1 points, or almost 1 percent, lower at 2,316.5, a rise of 2.6 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended weak in active trade, with the industrial and all-share indices shedding over 100 points in negative sentiment. Golds were softer ignoring a higher rand gold price. The Industrial index was off 132.2 points to 7,682.5, down 112.7 on the week, the all-share index lost 124.5 to 6,482.5, down 118.7 from last week, and golds were off 21.6 to 1,511.6, a fall of 16.4 for the week.
